subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers adopt or rebase the open conflicting fork PR, replace it with a fresh narrow same-repo fix, or close the fork PR before queueing another fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug and fix boundary are clear, but an open fork PR still uses closing syntax and is conflicting with current main, so automation should not create a competing fix PR until maintainers choose the branch path.

options.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
options.body: Close or supersede the stale conflicting fork branch and land a focused same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus sync and async displayName hydration.

options.title: Adopt/Rebase Fork PR
options.body: Have a maintainer or contributor update the fork PR to current main, add missing coverage and real behavior proof, then review it as the landing candidate.

options.title: Keep Waiting On Fork PR
options.body: Leave this issue blocked on the existing fork PR even though it is conflicting and has not updated since April 2026.

recommendation.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the stale conflicting fork branch and land a focused same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus sync and async displayName hydration.
